questions.q: What share of the world lived in extreme poverty about 200 years ago?
a: More than 90 percent
About 75 percent
Roughly half
Less than 10 percent
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts over 90 percent then with under 10 percent today.

questions.q: What does the Kuznets curve say happens to inequality as income grows?
a: It rises at first, peaks, then falls again
It falls steadily from the very start
It stays flat no matter how income grows
It rises continuously without ever reversing
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes inequality rising only initially, then declining.

questions.q: What did the Universal Declaration of Human Rights establish?
a: Certain non-negotiable rights for every person
A global trade agreement among nations
A shared budget for member countries
A permanent ban on war between states
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls it a humanist document granting every person non-negotiable rights.

questions.q: Why does the summary call Americans' fear of terrorism disproportionate?
a: Bee stings and lightning kill more Americans than attacks
Terror attacks have risen every year since 2001
The media refuses to report on terrorist attacks
Governments hide the true number of attacks
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes you are likelier to die from a bee sting or lightning.

questions.q: How does Pinker say we should face climate change and AI?
a: With reason and optimism, not conspiracy and fear
By trusting headlines to set the agenda
By waiting for technology to fix everything
By avoiding discussion of uncertain risks
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues these threats need proportion and rational thinking.
